issue.title: Flaky sase-core test: commit_at git fixture fails with 'fatal: could not parse HEAD'
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-g4.1 (epic sase-g4, plan-header validation) while landing that phase's sase-core release; not caused by that epic.

crates/sase_core/src/editor/completion.rs::tests::commit_inventory_skips_sidecars_before_reporting_the_row_cap failed in sase-core CI run 31099595038 with:

  git commit failed: fatal: could not parse HEAD

then passed on a re-run of the same tree, so it is a flake, not a regression.

The message is the assertion text in the test module's own commit_at() helper (completion.rs:3114-3118), which shells out to 'git -C <repo> commit --quiet --allow-empty -m <subject>' with GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE pinned. init_git_repo() (completion.rs:3083-3089) creates each repo with 'git init --quiet' plus user.name/user.email/core.abbrev config. This particular test is the heaviest fixture builder in the module: it creates ARTIFACT_REF_COMMIT_MAX_ROWS/ARTIFACT_REF_COMMIT_SCAN_LIMIT repos under one tempdir and commits ARTIFACT_REF_COMMIT_SCAN_LIMIT times into each, then adds a sidecar repo.

'fatal: could not parse HEAD' from 'git commit' means git resolved HEAD to a ref it could not read as a commit -- a partially written or truncated ref file, not a simply unborn HEAD (an unborn HEAD is the normal root-commit case and succeeds). Candidate causes worth checking: a ref write that lost a race with another cargo-test thread sharing the tempdir root, or a resource shortfall (ENOSPC / inode exhaustion) on the runner leaving a zero-length .git/refs entry -- the same class of runner resource problem that sase-fq.8 chased for the Python artifact-ref parity test, though the failing syscall and the failing test are different.

Scope: make the fixture deterministic against whatever the race is (e.g. assert on the ref after init, or serialize/retry the repo construction), or prove the cause and fix it at its source. Do not simply retry the whole test in CI.

Repo: sase-core (../sase-core via 'sase repo open sase-core), not this repo.
